Water Meter Leak: What It Means and Who Fixes It

By SRQ Leak Pros Editorial · Published November 5, 2026 · Updated November 7, 2026 · 6 min read

Short answer: A water meter leak shows up as water in the meter box, a soggy patch near the meter or a meter that spins when every tap is off. If the leak is at the meter or on the street side, it's usually the utility's to fix. If it's on the house side of the meter, it's usually yours. Call your utility first to check.

A water meter leak can mean three different things. The meter itself may be leaking, the pipe on the utility's side may be leaking, or the meter may be showing a leak somewhere in your home. If the leak is on your side, SRQ Leak Pros can connect you with a local provider for water service line repair in Sarasota.

This guide helps you sort out which one you have and who should fix it.

What does a water meter leak mean?

It depends on where the water is. Water inside the meter box or bubbling up next to it points to a leak at the meter, its fittings or nearby pipe. A dry meter box with a spinning flow indicator points to a leak downstream, somewhere in your plumbing.

What you seeLikely meaningWho to call first
Water pooling in the meter boxLeak at the meter, its fittings or the utility valveWater utility
Wet ground between meter and streetUtility side leakWater utility
Wet ground between meter and houseService line leak on your sideLeak detection or plumbing pro
Dry box, flow indicator spinsLeak inside the home or yardLeak detection or plumbing pro
Cracked meter lid or glassDamaged meterWater utility

How to test for a leak at the water meter

The EPA suggests a simple meter test. Read the meter, use no water for two hours, then read it again. If the numbers moved, you have a leak.

  1. Turn off all water use. Taps, sprinklers, ice maker, pool autofill and washer.
  2. Open the meter lid carefully. Watch for insects and standing water.
  3. Watch the flow indicator. On many meters it's a small triangle, star or dial.
  4. Note the reading. Snap a photo of the dial or display.
  5. Wait two hours. Use no water at all.
  6. Read it again. Any change means water is leaving the system.

To narrow it further, close your main shut-off valve at the house and watch the meter again. If the meter still moves, the leak is likely in the service line between the meter and the house. If it stops, the leak is inside the home.

Who is responsible for a water meter leak?

In most Sarasota-area utilities, the meter and the pipe on the street side belong to the utility. The service line on the house side of the meter belongs to the owner. Sarasota County's leak FAQ says its staff check reported leaks and decide whether each one is the county's or the customer's. The City of Sarasota Utilities Department runs water service within city limits. If you're unsure which utility serves you, check your bill.

Call your utility before anyone digs near the meter. They can tell you which side the leak is on and may shut off service at the curb stop if needed.

What causes a leak at the water meter?

  • Worn gaskets or washers at the meter couplings
  • A cracked meter body or register
  • A failing curb stop or meter valve
  • Shifting soil that strains the pipe at the box
  • Damage from mowers, vehicles or digging
  • An old service line joint just past the meter

Does a leak on the meter side affect my bill?

A leak before the meter usually doesn't register on your bill, because the water hasn't passed through the meter. A leak after the meter does. That's why a high bill paired with a dry meter box points to a leak in your plumbing. Some utilities offer a leak adjustment after you repair a customer-side leak. Rules vary, so ask your utility.

How priority works when you report a leak

Sarasota County's leak FAQ explains that customers without water are a high priority for its crews. It treats reduced pressure that stays above 20 psi as a lower, medium priority. When you call, describe what you see: water in the box, a wet patch, low pressure or no water at all.

Florida and federal rules that touch your meter

Federal rules under 40 CFR § 141.84 require water systems to keep a service line inventory. The inventory covers both the utility's part of the line and the customer's part. If your utility contacts you about your line material, that rule is the reason. On the customer side, Florida places service line repair within a plumbing contractor's scope.

Sarasota meter box tips

Sarasota meter boxes sit at ground level, often near the street or sidewalk. Summer storms can fill them with rainwater, which looks like a leak. Wait a dry day and check again before you call. Fire ants and wasps like meter boxes too, so lift the lid with care.

How to prevent meter area leaks

  • Keep the lid closed and clear so the utility can read it.
  • Don't plant shrubs or set pavers over the box.
  • Mark the box so mowers and vehicles avoid it.
  • Fix a dripping hose bib or toilet so the meter isn't masking a bigger leak.
  • Check the flow indicator once a month.

Local note: many North Port homes have long runs from the meter, so a slow leak can hide in the yard. In Osprey and Nokomis, rainy months can flood meter boxes and mask a real leak.

Related reading: if the meter test points to a buried leak, learn the signs of a water service line leak. A high bill is often the first clue, so see why your water bill is so high. Yards with sprinklers should also check for an irrigation leak, and pool owners can run a pool bucket test. Weak flow too? See why water pressure gets low.

When should you call a leak detection professional?

Call a pro when:

  • The meter moves with the main shut-off closed
  • You see a wet patch between the meter and the house
  • Your bill jumped and you can't find a leak inside
  • The utility says the leak is on your side

Frequently asked questions

Can a water meter leak inside the box?

Yes. Worn couplings or a cracked meter can leak into the box. Report it to your utility, which usually owns the meter.

Will the utility fix a leak at my meter?

Usually, if the leak is at the meter or on the street side. Leaks on the house side of the meter are usually the owner's to repair.

Why is my meter box full of water?

It may be rainwater, a leak at the meter, or a leak in the pipe nearby. Check on a dry day and watch the flow indicator with all water off.

Can a water meter be wrong?

Meters can fail, but most high readings trace to a real leak. Run the two-hour test first, then ask the utility to check the meter.
